content.text:
The spec already described git status colours for the file tree, but the code never had them, so I built them. Files and folders are now coloured by their git status. 100 of 101 tests pass, including two new ones; the one failure is the palette test that was already failing. `piton check` and `piton build check` pass. I haven't looked at the colours in the running app, so check they read well in both themes.

**Colours:**

| Status | Colour |
|---|---|
| Modified (renames count as modified) | amber |
| Added (staged new file) | green |
| Untracked | teal |
| Conflicted | red |
| Ignored, and everything inside an ignored folder | dimmed grey |
| Unchanged | normal |

- **Themes:** each colour uses a darker shade in light mode and a lighter one in dark mode, so it stays readable in both.
- **Folders:** a folder takes the most pressing status of anything inside it (conflicted, then modified, added, untracked), so a collapsed folder still shows there's a change.

**Refreshing:**
- **How:** it runs `git status` when the project opens, then every 2 seconds, and repaints only when something changed. That catches saving an edit, staging, committing and switching branches, including in folders you've never expanded.
- **Trade-off:** in a very large repository, a `git status` every couple of seconds could get noticeable. Hooking it to the file watcher instead would be more work.
- **Outside a repository**, or without git installed, nothing is coloured.

**Tests:**
- One reads sample `git status` output, covering every kind of change, renames, ignored folders and folders taking their contents' status.
- The other creates a real temporary repository, commits, edits a file, adds an untracked file and an ignored folder, and checks the statuses read back.

**Code:** the status reading is in a new `src/git_status.rs`, and the tree colours names with it in `src/project_tree.rs`.

**Spec:** I added the specific colours, that everything inside an ignored folder is dimmed, that renames count as modified, and that changes show within a couple of seconds.

- **How:** it runs `git status` when the project opens, then every 2 seconds, and repaints only when something changed. That catches saving an edit, staging, committing and switching branches, including in folders you've never expanded.
- **Trade-off:** in a very large repository, a `git status` every couple of seconds could get noticeable. Hooking it to the file watcher instead would be more work.
- **Outside a repository**, or without git installed, nothing is coloured.

**Tests:**
- One reads sample `git status` output, covering every kind of change, renames, ignored folders and folders taking their contents' status.
- The other creates a real temporary repository, commits, edits a file, adds an untracked file and an ignored folder, and checks the statuses read back.

**Code:** the status reading is in a new `src/git_status.rs`, and the tree colours names with it in `src/project_tree.rs`.

**Spec:** I added the specific colours, that everything inside an ignored folder is dimmed, that renames count as modified, and that changes show within a couple of seconds.
